answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with vested work bonds: every identity must lock a deposit that only unlocks after a thread of verified, useful jobs, each checked by independent peers. A newcomer starts on a bare knoll with no reputation and must pay the full bond plus weeks of real work before earning anything. A hollow identity with no history earns nothing, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds and a thousand work histories - far more than any single fake identity could ever repay.
